name: NY-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+24 partisan lean makes a Republican win structurally improbable
Hakeem Jeffries is an incumbent House Democratic leader who has raised $17.9 million with $4.2 million on hand
Republican Lewis Mizrahi shows no reported fundraising or outside spending support
Prediction markets price the Democratic side at roughly 97 percent
model.rationale: The district's D+24 lean, Jeffries' incumbency and national profile, and his overwhelming financial advantage leave no realistic path for the Republican challenger, who shows no measurable fundraising or outside backing. Markets price this race at about 97 percent Democratic, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: Only a major external shock to Jeffries' candidacy or an unexpectedly well-funded challenger effort would put this race in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic incumbent and House party leader, seeks another term in a Brooklyn-based district with a D+24 partisan lean. He has raised nearly $18 million and holds $4.2 million on hand, while Republican challenger Lewis Mizrahi reports no fundraising and draws no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets put Jeffries' chances near 97 percent.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but the structural fundamentals leave little ambiguity. A first-time Republican candidate with no visible financial operation faces a well-known incumbent in heavily Democratic territory. The expected margin is a comfortable Democratic win, and the main uncertainty is only how large the victory will be, not who prevails.
